checks.message: EFS file system not encrypted at rest
checks.context: Encryption must be set at creation time because you can't enable it on an existing file system. An unencrypted EFS volume containing application data, configs, or secrets is a compliance failure waiting to happen.

checks.message: Verify the file system policy restricts access to specific VPCs or IAM principals
checks.context: Without a resource policy, any EC2 instance that can reach the mount target can mount the file system. Lock it down with a policy that requires specific IAM roles or VPC conditions.

checks.message: Verify the mount target security group restricts NFS (port 2049) to only trusted sources
checks.context: NFS has no built-in authentication. If port 2049 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 or a broad CIDR, any host that can reach the mount target can mount your file system and read all data.

checks.message: EFS deletion is permanent. All data is destroyed
checks.context: There is no recycle bin for EFS. All files, directories, and metadata are gone. You must delete all mount targets before you can delete the file system.

checks.message: Verify the policy doesn't grant public access via Principal: *
checks.context: An EFS resource policy with Principal: * allows any AWS principal to mount the file system. This is almost never intentional and exposes all file system data.
